articles.title: ClauseClear: Gemma 3 1B flags the risky clauses in your client contract, privately
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle ClauseClear is a local contract checklist for freelancers. You drop in a client agreement (PDF or paste). A Gemm…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built ClauseClear is a local contract checklist for freelancers. You drop in a client agreement (PDF or paste). A Gemma 3 1B model running in Ollama on this laptop returns the clauses worth negotiating: payment, IP, exclusivity, termination, late fees, scope, liability. Each finding has to carry a verbatim quote . If Gemma paraphrases, ClauseClear snaps the claim back to the nearest real sentence — or marks it review and retries. Then it drafts the email you send the client. The PDF never leaves the machine. There is no account. There is no cloud LLM. Who would pay: a solo designer, developer, or illustrator staring at a five-page "standard" contractor agreement the night before kickoff.

articles.excerpt: I Put My Own Product Through a Colonoscopy and Found 260 Things Or: how one human, ~80 AI sub-agents across ten fleets, and a graph database that occasionally changed its personality taught me what "p…
articles.body: I Put My Own Product Through a Colonoscopy and Found 260 Things Or: how one human, ~80 AI sub-agents across ten fleets, and a graph database that occasionally changed its personality taught me what "production-grade" actually means. Mostly by violating it first. The Pitch, or: Why I Built a Sword When Everyone Else Sells Maps Every identity breach you've read about — Storm-0558, MGM, Snowflake — was not a hack . It was a walk . Somebody got one credential, opened their favorite graph tool, followed the pretty attack-path arrows to Domain Admin, and the arrows did not fight back. The tools that exist will happily draw you a beautiful map of your own destruction and then leave for lunch. BloodHound shows you the path. Nobody swings the sword.

articles.title: Athena: A Local-First Git & AST Change-Intelligence Engine and MCP Server
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Most release-note generators and PR review bots do the same thing: they dump git log --oneline into a cloud LLM…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built Most release-note generators and PR review bots do the same thing: they dump git log --oneline into a cloud LLM and hope for the best. That fails in real engineering teams for two reasons: Commit messages lie. A commit titled fix(api): minor cleanup in parameter defaults might actually insert an optional parameter before an existing one ( def compute(a, b=2) -> def compute(a, inserted=0, b=2) ), silently shifting positional arguments for every caller in production. Hallucinations & privacy. Cloud LLMs invent commit hashes, miss downstream callers, and require sending proprietary source diffs to external APIs.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
